result.title: FrontierRefactor: Benchmarking Multi-Scale Performance-Oriented Codebase Refactoring
result.summary: Autonomous codebase refactoring requires coding agents to restructure working software while strictly preserving externally observable behavior and prioritizing execution performance and compute efficiency over stylistic preference. Existing benchmarks: refactoring benchmarks assess functional correctness while overlooking runtime regressions, whereas code performance benchmarks target isolated micro-kernels that ignore codebase-scale complexity. We observe that refactoring scale is governed by the scope of the observable contract, the caller-visible interface fixing behavioral invariants while freeing private implementations for optimization. Building on this insight, we introduce FrontierRefactor, a benchmark of 60 qualified engineering tasks spanning four scales, from computational kernels to full repositories, across in-place optimization and cross-language rewriting. Evaluating frontier coding agents through a reference-free cascaded protocol across 1,080 execution runs reveals that correctness and speedup are largely decoupled: 41.2% of submissions satisfy functional equivalence yet fail to deliver verified performance improvements, with 19.3% suffering performance regressions and 21.9% trapped in measurement noise. Refactoring paradigms reveal orthogonal engineering bottlenecks: while cross-language rewrites gain speedups from native compilation after passing functional checks, agents struggle with contract fidelity, with pass rates dropping from 65.0% on modules to 32.6% at package scale; conversely, in-place optimization reliably preserves behavioral contracts at 86.5% but rarely achieves acceleration without physical performance profiling. Trajectory analysis shows that agents fall victim to uncalibrated micro-benchmarking illusions, an operational blind spot that multi-turn execution-timing feedback directly resolves, raising strict success from 16.0% to 40.0%.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文提出 FrontierRefactor，一个面向代码库重构的基准，覆盖从计算内核到完整仓库的四种规模、60 个任务，并用级联协议评估前沿编码智能体在功能等价与执行性能上的表现。
AI.relevance_reason: 研究问题为代码重构的正确性与加速评测，既无视觉/多模态输入，也不涉及内部推理状态、视觉证据或 latent 生成，与 LVR 主线缺少可核查的实质联系，仅多轮执行计时反馈与智能体循环有点表面相似，不足以构成借鉴线索。
